operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
as President of the United States, and by 
the Communications Act of 1934 (48 Stat. 
1064), as amended, it is ordered that Ex­
ecutive Order No.
operative_clauses.quote_continuation:
of September 24, 
1940, creating the Defense Communica­
tions Board and defining its functions 
and duties, be, and it is hereby, amended 
by substituting for the words “Assistant 
Secretary of the Treasury in Charge of 
the Coast Guard”, wherever they appear 
in the said order, the words “Assistant 
Secretary of the Treasury in Charge of 
Treasury Enforcement Activities” .
operative_clauses.text_note: The number of the amended order (EO 8546) is printed with a footnote mark that the OCR joins to it; the quotation is split around that token and resumes in quote_continuation.

seeded_payload.research_rationale: EO 8960 (Dec. 6, 1941; 6 FR 6325) has one operative paragraph: it amends EO 8546 by substituting 'Assistant Secretary of the Treasury in Charge of Treasury Enforcement Activities' for the Assistant Secretary in charge of the Coast Guard wherever EO 8546 names him (Board membership and secretary). The substituted wording lived in EO 8546 until that order was revoked; EO 9183 (June 15, 1942) amended this order only by the Board's renaming. No expiry or condition. The orders rest on wartime and emergency powers (Communications Act sec. 606 and the national emergency); neither the orders nor sec. 606 had lapsed before Feb. 24, 1947: the state of war declared in December 1941 had not been terminated, and no concurrent resolution ending the sec. 606 powers is recorded in the bounded sources; no earlier presidential order ending any of these provisions appears in the OFR catalog or the saved order texts. EO 9831 para. 2 revokes EO 8960 together with EO 8546, effective on issuance Feb. 24, 1947; first end of the clause and of the order: 1947-02-24. The 1989 Codification row: 'Amended EO 8546. Amended by EO 9183 ... Revoked by EO 9831'. No current-law citation.

savings_residuals.quote:
1. The Board of War Communica­
tions, established as the Defense Com­
munications Board by Executive Order 
No. 8546 of September 24, 1940, is abol­
ished, and all property and records 
thereof are transferred to the Federal 
Communications Commission.
savings_residuals.reason: EO 9831 para. 1 abolishes the Board of War Communications and transfers all its property and records to the Federal Communications Commission; para. 2 revokes the five orders without any savings clause. The Board's records and property pass to the FCC; claims to just compensation for any government use or control of facilities rest on Communications Act sec. 606 itself, not on the revoked orders. No continuing effect rests on this order.
